title: Headroom circuit-breaker, predictive autoscale, and post-incident remediation for Dedicated capacity shortfalls
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Design, implement, and validate a headroom-based circuit-breaker and short-horizon predictive autoscaling policy for Dedicated GPU pools to prevent capacity shortfalls that cause SLA violations. This ticket covers: (1) runtime policy changes to reject/newly-routed reserved requests when projected headroom < safety threshold, (2) a short-term traffic forecast model and warm-up reservation mechanism, (3) automatic throttles and graceful fallback to compatible hosted models, (4) observability (alerts/dashboards) and (5) post-incident remediation tasks and customer communication hooks. Goal: reduce frequency of incidents where pool saturation leads to >2x latency and customer error rates spike, and provide deterministic safe-fallback behavior for affected requests.
acceptance_criteria: Headroom circuit-breaker implemented at the fleet controller level and configurable per-pool
Predictive scaler runs every 15s and provides a 60s horizon forecast that reduces missed scale events by >=70% in replay tests
When projected headroom < configured threshold, new reserved requests are rejected with a clear error code and monitored metric; existing in-flight requests complete without failure
Fallback route to compatible hosted model triggers automatically for blocked requests and is tracked per-customer for billing/analytics
Runbook updated with step-by-step remediation, escalation, and customer communication templates
End-to-end synthetic test simulating 3x burst verifies no SLA breach for non-evicted reserved traffic in 90% of runs
tasks: Design API: pool-level "headroom" and "safe_reject" flags and policy contract
Implement fleet controller circuit-breaker hook and error code 429-Dedicated-Headroom
Build short-horizon traffic forecaster (15s cadence, 60s horizon) and integrate with scaler
Create warm-up reservation flow to temporarily reserve ephemeral instances for bursts
Implement hosted-model fallback routing and per-request telemetry tagging
Add dashboard panels: projected headroom, rejected-by-headroom, fallback-rate, latency-on-fallback
Write and validate runbook; add automated notification templates for customers
Load-test in staging and run chaos scenarios; produce findings

postmortem_action_items: Formalize headroom % defaults and rollout plan (PM + SRE decision)
Add per-customer fallback opt-out and billing reconciliation workflow
Instrument and retain 30d of headroom projections for drift analysis
Create monthly report on rejected requests and fallback success rate
Update customer SLA templates and status page incident messaging
mitigation_runbook: Page on-call: check fleet headroom dashboard and recent scale events
If projected headroom < threshold: enable pool-evacuation-mode to prevent new reservations and trigger warm-up reservations in adjacent pools
If latencies spike: execute rollback to previous autoscale policy and open emergency canary of hosted fallback for affected customers
Notify affected customers via automated template and open dedicated incident channel
Post-incident: capture snapshot of pool topology, scaler logs, and JSON of predictive forecasts for root-cause analysis
notes_tradeoffs: Rejecting new reservations reduces blast radius but can degrade customer experience; fallback routing mitigates but may increase per-token cost
Conservative headroom thresholds reduce incidents but lower utilization; plan to iterate using real traffic and cost telemetry
Short-horizon forecasting adds complexity and potential for false positives; chosen 60s horizon balances timeliness and signal-to-noise
Warm-up reservations consume headroom temporarily; will be capped per-customer to avoid abuse
